paper_title: Interleaving Retrieval with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for   Knowledge-Intensive Multi-Step Questions
caption: Number of questions, out of 40, where CoT generated by GPT3 using different methods has at least 1 factual error. Factual errors: < OneR < NoR.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the number of factual errors generated by a large language model using various methods on a set of knowledge-intensive multi-step questions. The horizontal axis represents question sources, labeled as HotpotQA, 2WikiMQA, MuSiQue, and IIRC, presented in that order from left to right. The vertical axis represents the count of questions with at least one factual error, ranging from 0 to 40 with tick labels at increments of 5. Three categories of question answering methods are represented by colored bars: NoR QA (orange), OneR QA (red), and IRCot QA (blue). The shortest bars, with a value of 5, are represented by the OneR QA method for HotpotQA and 2WikiMQA question sources. The tallest bar, with a value of 29, represents the NoR QA method for the HotpotQA question source. The OneR QA method for MuSiQue had a value of 23, while the IRCot QA method had a value of 15. The NoR QA method for 2WikiMQA and IIRC had a value of 28 and 14, respectively. The OneR QA method for IIRC had the lowest value of 11. Annotations displaying the exact values of each bar are positioned above each bar. The bars are not sorted in any specific order beyond the initial presentation of question sources on the horizontal axis, and no bars are visually emphasized.
